meta.title: Safeguards — what BellumAI will not do in your place
meta.description: Laura drafts, you decide. The safeguards behind that promise live in the code, not in a brochure.

hero.title: What we will not do in your place.
hero.lead: Sales software can write to your clients faster than you can. The real question is not whether it is able to — it is what stops it. This page describes what BellumAI refuses to do, and what, inside the product, stops it.

copilot.title: Laura drafts. You send.
copilot.paragraph: Laura is your sales intelligence copilot. She gathers, she cross-checks, she writes. She has no write path into your mailbox: when she suggests a message, she returns a proposal, and it is your own action that saves the draft. This is not a cautious setting someone could loosen — it is the absence of code.

items.label: No tool of Laura's can send.
items.desc: The step that prepares a message returns a proposal. There is no send call behind it, and therefore nothing to switch off.

items.label: The body of your messages never reaches the model.
items.desc: To draft a follow-up, Laura receives the counterpart, the subject line, and how long the conversation has been silent. Not the text of your exchanges.

guardrails.title: The six safeguards on automatic follow-ups
guardrails.paragraph: Only one family of automations reaches a client without a salesperson having clicked just before: follow-up reminders, and only if your workspace has armed them. Six safeguards hold them. No setting turns them off — the function that decides whether a follow-up may go out receives only the target's situation and the current time. There is no checkbox to bypass one.

items.label: A reply closes the sequence.
items.desc: The moment your counterpart replies, the follow-up stops — for good. It is the most important of the six: chasing someone who has just replied is the fastest way to be ignored.

items.label: One follow-up, never a cadence.
items.desc: One automatic message per target and per rule, at most. No escalation, no five-step sequence, no copying in the manager on the third round. Whatever is still unanswered after one follow-up goes back to being a human matter.

items.label: Opt-out is re-read on every send.
items.desc: Never from a cache. An opt-out recorded yesterday applies to today's message, and the check is redone target by target.

items.label: Quiet hours.
items.desc: Nothing before 8:00, nothing after 19:00, nothing at the weekend. An automatic sales email arriving on a Sunday in the middle of the night is noticed — and it tells its recipient that no human read it first.

items.label: A cap per workspace, per day.
items.desc: 25 automatic follow-ups at most. A loop that runs away stops on a number, not on somebody's vigilance on a Friday evening.

items.label: Nothing is armed by default.
items.desc: Every automatic follow-up stays off until a human in your workspace turns it on, and a single action turns everything off again.

review.title: And even armed, a follow-up is put to you.
review.paragraph: The six safeguards answer the question "can this target be chased?". They do not answer "can this particular text go to this particular client today?". That is a different question, and a human answers it.

items.label: What you read is what goes out.
items.desc: Subject and body are frozen at the moment the request is put to you. Nothing is recomposed at approval time: approving one text and sending another would be worse than showing nothing.

items.label: A refusal holds for good.
items.desc: For that target, the follow-up you refused will not be put to you again the next day. Otherwise the only way out would be to disarm the whole automation.

items.label: An undecided request expires.
items.desc: After 3 days it does not go out. A follow-up prepared last week speaks of a silence that may no longer exist.

refusals.title: What this page does not do either.
refusals.paragraph: A page explaining what we refuse to do is judged first on what it allows itself to write.

items.label: No market figures.
items.desc: We were offered unsubscribe and sender-reputation statistics to back this page up. We could not tie them to a public source, named and dated. So they are not here: the only numbers written on this page are constants of the product.

items.label: No delivery dates.
items.desc: What this page describes works today. What does not exist yet is not announced, not even approximately.

items.label: No competitor names.
items.desc: We name capabilities — your mailbox, your CRM, your calendar — never other people's tools, and never to compare ourselves to them.

cta.paragraph: The demo shows the product as it is, on a dataset labelled as fictional.
